title: C-Sections Just Passed Natural Births In Brazil
source: Brazil's cesarean-section share of live births, compiled from peer-reviewed trend analyses (Medicine journal, 'Cesarean section rates in Brazil') and Brazilian Ministry of Health/DATASUS birth records: the national C-section rate rose from about 15% in 1970 to roughly 38% by 2001 and 48.4% by 2008, then crossed 50% in the early 2010s to reach 55.4% in 2016 and 57.2% in 2020 -- one of the highest national rates in the world, and now the more common way Brazilian babies are born.
